# Card 4 (interaction) — strategist, 2026-11-21 (saved by Jarvis; the agent cannot write files)

Path to Exile in, Talisman of Creativity out. Runner-up Counterspell, same slot. Read: context, Krenko/Magda/Teval/Purphoros NOTES.md, interaction-suite + ratios sections, every candidate and cut's oracle text.
- Path: the shape that covers most of what killed the deck — Krenko, Teval, Magda's dragons are creatures; one-mana instant lets him answer on sight AND land Shabraz the same turn (008: held Swords + a 2-mana spell and passed — a one-mana answer shrinks that tradeoff). strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite: breadth then depth, copy the answer your table beats you with; removal 6 (with Kozilek's) is short of Walser's 8-10; Path → 7, suite 10 with counters, inside Hinds' 7-15; voltron protection budget 6-8 met. strategy:deckbuilding.ratios: derive from failure modes — removal is the failure mode.
- Path needs W (thinnest); cutting Creativity leaves W16 untouched. 7th rock the cheapest slot; rocks before lands; 37 lands stay.
- Rejected: Dovin's Veto / An Offer (noncreature only; killers are creature spells; Offer gives Treasures); Arcane Denial (two cards to the opponent, wrong side of an out-draw plan); Generous Gift (third catch-all at 3, gives a 3/3); Blasphemous Act (kills Shabraz, Brallin and the Humans; indestructible cover is for Shabraz, not a wipe; Kozilek's is the right size).
- Dissent: NO CHANGE defensible (10 pieces in range; 008 a play error). Path gives a land; Counterspell doesn't and stops Teval/Krenko on the way in, but UU held up fights the tempo problem and does nothing against the live Altar loop. Path can't touch Purphoros or the Altar — Chaos Warp / Get Lost are the real outs. Will of the Jeskai a reasonable alternative cut (symmetric wheel), left.
Open: research-strategy topic — one-mana interaction vs holding up mana in a tempo-slow commander deck.

contributions.text:
Asked: does the branch need a ninth interaction card, and if so which shape. Answer: Path to Exile in, Mask of Memory out; contested, and NO CHANGE is a defensible floor. The branch audit reads interaction at 8, exactly Walser's floor (Collective Defiance, Get Lost, Kozilek's Return, Negate, Prismari Command, Stubborn Denial, Swords to Plowshares, Voracious Greatshark), with an interactive suite of 17 copies; no logged game on v3.0.0 was lost for want of an answer in the 99 (008 had Swords in hand; 009 was a thin keep), so the premise 'the deck lacks interaction' is the recon's consensus gap, not a log finding. What actually kills this deck is a creature on the battlefield: enumerating every killer the eight A-team NOTES and decklists and the log name (Krenko, Tannuk, Teval, Magda, Wilhelt, Neyith, Zur, Purphoros, Utvara Hellkite, Blood Artist, Gravecrawler, Phyrexian Altar, Sundial of the Infinite) gives thirteen objects, eleven of them creature cards, two artifacts, and no instant or sorcery. A hard counter answers eleven of the thirteen only on the way in and none of them once landed (Krenko's tap, the Altar and Sundial activations, Teval's trigger are abilities; Utvara is tutored onto the battlefield, never cast), and it needs two blue held through three opponents' turns in a deck whose own turn is a five-mana Shabraz or a sorcery-speed wheel. A one-mana instant exile answers ten of the thirteen on the board, sits beside the Shabraz turn on six mana, costs the colour with slack (white 24 of 22), and is the shape the pilot already held and should have cast in 008. Blasphemous Act is refused: it deals 13 to Shabraz and every Human, and only five cards in the list (Flawless Maneuver, Loran's Escape, Akroma's Will, Slip Out the Back, Shelter) keep him through it; Kozilek's Return, already in, is the wipe this list can afford, since both commanders at 3 toughness survive it. Mask is the cut because it is the duplicated function (Q046 decided Enduring Curiosity does its job for every creature) and colourless, so the swap moves no source; it is the pilot's own 2026-10-01 add, so contested.
